description: The chart illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) relative to the Whisper large‑v3 baseline after cumulative automated optimisation steps, shown for two fine-tuned models. The category axis is vertical (y-axis) and is labeled “Optimisations applied,” listing five optimisation steps in top-to-bottom order: “Normalised,” “Add Spacing,” “Remove Spacing,” “Americanisms,” and “Dates.” The value axis is horizontal (x-axis) and is labeled “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large,” using a linear numeric scale with tick labels shown at approximately 0.000, 0.001, 0.002, and 0.003 (range extending slightly beyond 0.003 to accommodate the longest bars). Each category contains a pair of horizontally oriented bars: an orange bar for the “NESAC ft model” and a green bar for the “SESHA ft model,” as indicated by the legend titled “Model” below the plot. For “Normalised,” the orange NESAC bar is labeled 0.00334 and the green SESHA bar is labeled 0.00323; for “Add Spacing,” the orange bar is 0.00319 and the green bar is 0.00344; for “Remove Spacing,” the orange bar is 0.00311 and the green bar is 0.00306; for “Americanisms,” the orange bar is 0.00299 and the green bar is 0.00302; and for “Dates,” the orange bar is 0.00257 and the green bar is 0.00228. Numeric value labels are printed at the right end of each bar, and the bars are grouped by optimisation step without stacking, with no additional visual emphasis such as outlines or annotations beyond the value labels.
